claims.evidence: Fix an admissible p and let t be its guaranteed capture time. Every grid vertex must lie within initial graph distance t of some zombie; otherwise a survivor starting there and remaining stationary cannot be reached in t zombie moves. Each Cartesian-grid radius-t ball is contained in an L∞ cube with at most (2t+1)^k vertices, so n^k≤p(2t+1)^k. With x=p+t, p≤x and 2t+1≤3x because p≥1, hence n^k≤3^k x^(k+1) and x≥3^(-k/(k+1))n^(k/(k+1)). This holds for every admissible p and survives minimization in the throttling definition.
claims.search_method: Direct reconstruction of the covering argument from the game rules, including initial placement, stationary-survivor timing, ball cardinality, and minimization quantifiers.

claims.claim: Mesh capture lemma: for each r≥1 there are constants M_r,A_r such that, on every r-dimensional Cartesian grid with coordinate meshes containing both endpoints and having gaps at most d, placing M_r zombies at every mesh intersection guarantees capture in at most A_r d rounds.
claims.evidence: The induction is complete. In dimension one, consecutive mesh zombies bracket any survivor not initially on the mesh, and their separation contracts until capture within d rounds. For dimension r, take R=A_{r-1}d. On each side in every coordinate, either the relevant boundary is within R or the gap condition gives a mesh hyperplane at distance in [R,R+d). Multiplicity M_r=2rM_{r-1} permits disjoint labeled projected teams on all 2r planes. Each projected move changes a non-i coordinate toward the survivor and therefore is a legal full L1-shortest-path move. The induction hypothesis produces an aligned i-guard within R rounds. A nonboundary plane cannot be reached earlier than the last survivor move of that interval; if reached on that last move, the move is in coordinate i, leaves the projection unchanged, and encounters the already aligned guard. Boundary planes cannot be crossed. After establishment, a guard repairs the sole projected mismatch caused by the preceding survivor move, or advances in coordinate i when no mismatch exists, so it cannot be crossed without capture. One further zombie turn synchronizes all guards. Thereafter, the sum W of lower-to-upper guard separations is initially below 2r(R+d) and falls by at least 2 on every noncapture round: the pair in the survivor's moved coordinate advances while other guards repair that coordinate. Capture follows within r(R+d) additional rounds. Finally R+1+r(R+d)≤(r+1)(A_{r-1}+1)d for integral d≥1, so the stated recurrence supplies constants depending only on r. Degenerate coordinates result in earlier capture.
claims.search_method: Adversarial induction audit of team multiplicity, projected-move legality, last-round plane crossing, persistent guard invariants, synchronization, and the integer separation potential.

claims.claim: Consequently, for every fixed k≥3, th_z((P_n)^{□k})=Θ_k(n^{k/(k+1)})=Θ_k(|G|^{1/(k+1)}); in particular the k=3 endpoint is complete.
claims.evidence: For d=ceil(n^(k/(k+1))), the endpoint-augmented coordinate mesh has gaps at most d and at most n/d+2≤n^(1/(k+1))+2 points. The mesh lemma therefore uses O_k((n/d+2)^k)=O_k(n^(k/(k+1))) zombies and O_k(d)=O_k(n^(k/(k+1))) rounds. The zombie count is at most n^k for all sufficiently large n; the finitely many remaining n are legitimately absorbed into the fixed-k constant by occupying every vertex. Claim 0 supplies the matching lower bound. Since |G|=n^k, the requested exponent is exactly |G|^(1/(k+1)). The recurrences give M_2=4, A_2=6, M_3=24, and A_3=28, so k=3 is explicitly included.
claims.search_method: Exact symbolic substitution into the mesh bound, exponent comparison, admissibility check for the zombie count, finite-small-n fallback, and direct recurrence arithmetic for k=3.

target_evidence: The exact target asks whether the Cartesian k-grid has zombie-throttling number Θ(|G|^(1/(k+1))) for every fixed k≥3, with a complete k=3 endpoint. The verified covering argument proves the required lower bound, and the verified mesh lemma plus the chosen mesh scale proves the matching upper bound for every fixed k≥3. The identity |G|=n^k converts the n-exponent to the requested vertex-count exponent, and the explicit k=3 constants complete the stated first endpoint. Thus the draft's FULL resolution claim is accurate rather than broader or weaker than the target.
